---

## 1. Requirement Overview

The Flat Wire Mill module is the **shopfloor and dashboard layer** for three new Flattening Lines — FL1,
FL2 and the hybrid FL3 — converting aluminium rod into coreless oscillated flat wire coils. It is a new
capability inside the existing UAL Manufacturing Execution System, not a standalone application.

**Size, as measured in the analysis, not quoted from a header:**

| Measure | Count |
|---|---|
| Defined `FR-###` requirements | **424** |
| Non-functional requirements with a measurable target | **10** (`NFR003`–`NFR007`, `NFR009`–`NFR013`) |
| Non-functional targets **undefined in every source** | **4** (AGC sample rate, concurrent clients, latency budget, `RunReading` retention) |
| `[PROPOSED]` — written by the delivery team, never client-reviewed | **69** |
| Deferred to MVP-2 | **75** |
| Withdrawn by client decision (4 Aug 2026) | **27** |
| Known-unimplementable as written | **6** |
| Screens / dashboards in scope | **24** |

**Two properties make this module unlike every other UAL shopfloor module, and both drive test depth:**

1. **The Pass Schedule is the machine's brain.** One configuration record decides which components are
   active or bypassed, the die sizes, the roll clearances, the edge configuration, the gauge and width
   targets and the route mode. **Operator acknowledgement of that record at check-in is what pushes PLC
   tags to the line.** Nothing runs without it, and nothing else configures the machine.
2. **Weld genealogy is a contractual deliverable.** Welding-wire customers require a traceable chain
   from supplier heat, through every rod-to-rod induction weld, to the finished coil alpha, with footage
   attribution per source rod. `NFR012` is a customer obligation, not an internal quality goal.

**Derived behaviour** *(logically entailed by the requirements, not stated as requirements)*:

- Because `FR-049` bans a PLC write at pre-check-in and `FR-391` bans one during schedule generation,
  **check-in acknowledgement is the only write path to the machine** — so it is the only place a
  configuration defect can enter, and the only place to test for one.
- Because a rod stays mounted across an order boundary (`FR-548`) and a check-in points at exactly one
  run, **one run can span two orders** — so any assertion keyed on `FlatWireRun.OrderId` is unsafe at a
  boundary.
- Because `FR-013` closes an MMS ID strictly on consumption and `FR-009` sets ITInhibit when no MMS ID
  is active, **a gap between close and re-open would inhibit a healthy line** — so the weld transition
  must be tested for continuity, not only for correctness.

**Assumptions** *(the analysis's `RA-ASM##`, carried, not resolved)*: pass schedules are authored outside
MVP-1's delivered UI; an operator is physically present at every transaction; one skid is open per line at
a time; `FL{n}.LineState` is readable while faulted.

**Missing information** *(recorded, not filled)*: the 14 Critical clarifications `RA-Q01`–`RA-Q14`, the
four undefined NFR targets, and the `Q41` question underneath all of FL2 pre-check-in.

## 2. Business Objective

| # | Objective | What testing must prove |
|---|---|---|
| **BO1** | **Lower unit cost than pancake coils**, opening the welding-wire market | That a coil completes with a correct derived weight, a valid skid pairing and a printable label — the chain that makes a coil sellable |
| **BO2** | **Weld genealogy as a contractual deliverable** | That the chain `coil alpha → non-overlapping footage ranges → rod alpha → supplier heat` reconstructs completely for a **multi-rod, multi-coil** run. A single-rod run does not exercise it |
| **BO3** | **Represent rod, flattening, bundle width, edge type and coreless coils in the MES** | That the shared-schema write-backs land in existing columns, all-or-nothing, and that a retry does not duplicate |
| **BO4** | **Operator execution and machine configuration on the floor** | That the acknowledgement → PLC push path configures the machine correctly, and that every gate that exists to stop bad material actually stops it |

**The quality objective that outranks the others:** the module drives a physical machine at production
speed. A defect in the configuration push does not produce a wrong screen — it produces **wrong product,
by the thousand feet, under a certificate that says it is right.**

## 4. Requirement Understanding

### 4.1 The three routes, and why each needs its own coverage

| Route | Path | Gauge trace | Key differences that change test design |
|---|---|---|---|
| **FL1** standalone | rod → wire drawing (DB1/DB2) → 12″ mill FM1 → intermediate spool | **Real-time** | **No edger.** Produces a spool, not a coil. Two payoff bays with welding between rods |
| **FL2** standalone | pre-flattened spool → finishing mill FM2 (S1 8″, S2 6″, S3 6″) → coreless coil | **Real-time, at a 4 s update rate** — from the gauging stands downstream of S3 ✅ *`G120` resolved 9 Sep 2026: `A3` retired, `FR-120` superseded. ⚠ Five P1 cases invert — see `TC-140`/`141`/`492`, widen `TC-494`* | **No drawing dies**, so no die change. One traversing payoff. Edgers at S2 and S3; **S3 is final and non-bypassable** |
| **FL3** hybrid | FL1 feeding FL2 continuously, no intermediate anneal | **Real-time** | **No intermediate spool, no spool alpha, no FL2 check-in step** ⚠ *disputed, `OI-09`*. One acknowledgement pushes FM1 **and** FM2 — across **two controllers**, `G99` |

**Consequence for planning:** a scenario proven on FL1 does **not** transfer to FL2 or FL3. The three
routes differ in what exists (edger, dies, spool), in what is broadcast (live vs null), and in how many
controllers a single acknowledgement writes to. Route is therefore a **coverage dimension**, not a
parameter.

### 4.2 What the module is a gatekeeper for

The register is unusually rich in **gates** — points where the system exists to stop something. Each is a
separate test responsibility because each has a stated bypass rule:

| Gate | Rule | Bypass |
|---|---|---|
| Staging inspection fail | Hard block; only forward action is WIP Rejection | **None** (`FR-041`) |
| Check-in inspection fail | Hard block, routed to WIP Rejection | **None** (`FR-068`) |
| Machine-inspection step fail | Rod on hold | Supervisor override with badge, password, reason (`FR-081`) |
| Pre-run SPC out of spec | Acknowledge button disabled | **None stated** (`FR-069`) |
| SPC out of spec, in run | Material to SPC-HOLD, **machine keeps running** | Force-continue **always available** (`FR-186`) |
| Stop transaction without SPC | Update disabled | **None** — readings need not be in spec (`FR-274`) |
| Spool alpha issue | Per-spool SPC mandatory | **None** (`FR-157`) |
| Checkout while line running | Blocked on `LineState` | **None**; the system never stops the line (`FR-301`, `FR-302`) |
| Mid-run checkout finalisation | Supervisor approval | **None** (`FR-323`) ⚠ unenforced in MVP-1 |
| Weld quality Fail | Logged, flagged, may pause | **Does not block the run** (`FR-168`) |
| Order boundary | Operator marks the order complete | **None** — no auto-close (`FR-552`) |

**A gate with no bypass and a gate with a bypass are different tests.** The negative case for a
no-bypass gate is *"prove no control exists"* — `FR-043` makes this explicit by requiring the fresh-start
control to be **absent from the DOM**, not merely disabled.

### 4.3 Where truth lives

| Value | Authoritative source | Why it matters to testing |
|---|---|---|
| Footage | **PLC counter**, read and locked at dialog open | Never typed (`FR-162`, `FR-303`). A test that types footage tests nothing |
| Timestamps | **Server-side at API receipt** | Never the client clock (`FR-174`). Clock-skew tests are meaningful |
| Weight | **Derived** from footage × cross-section × density | Never a scale during rolling (`FR-015`); a scale may override **at completion only** |
| Density ρ | `united_db..alloys.alloy_density` | Cross-database read |
| Payoff occupancy | **`RodStaging`**, not `PayoffWeight` | `FR-424` — a zero sensor reading and an empty bay are different states |
| Alloy max reduction | `united_db..alloys.Draw_max_reduction` | **Not** the `AlloyProperty` seed (`OI-93`) |
| Machine configuration | The acknowledged **Pass Schedule** | The only write path |

### 4.4 What the analysis found that changes the shape of testing

1. **Six requirements cannot be tested at all as written** — `FR-280`–`FR-282` (no host), `FR-297` (no
   column), `FR-563` (blocked on `Q87`), `FR-175` (no host). They are planned as **Not Testable** with
   the reason, not omitted.
2. **Two requirements are self-contradictory with a sibling** — `FR-045`/`FR-546` (refuse vs authorise)
   and `FR-034`/`FR-106` (absolute pounds vs percent bands). **No scenario can assert an outcome** until
   they are resolved; both are planned as coverage-blocked with a clarification.
3. **One requirement is arithmetically self-defeating** — `FR-153`'s ±2 %. This is planned as a
   **deliberate failing scenario** (`SC-072`), because the evidence that the threshold is wrong is a test
   that fails on conforming material.
4. **Authorisation is specified and not enforced.** Planned as a negative assertion (`SC-158`) so the
   condition is demonstrated rather than assumed.

## 5. Business Rules

Rules extracted from the requirements, grouped by trigger. **Rule violations are listed because each is a
negative test responsibility.**

### 5.1 Machine configuration

| Rule | Trigger | Influencing data | Roles | Expected behaviour | Violation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **BR-01** Only acknowledgement pushes tags | Operator confirms the schedule at check-in | Pass schedule, payoff position | Operator | One batch: component flags, die sizes, roll gaps, gauge/width targets | A push at pre-check-in (`FR-049`) or during generation (`FR-391`) |
| **BR-02** Records before the push, always | Acknowledgement | Inspection, SPC, schedule ID + version + effective date | System | All audit records persisted **before** the PLC write; recovery marker retained on write failure | A push with no preceding record |
| **BR-03** Failure re-clears, it does not roll back | Any individual tag write fails | Tags already written | System | Compensating re-clear + revert shared-schema changes + abort | Treating it as an ACID rollback |
| **BR-04** FL3 pushes both mills in one acknowledgement | FL3 check-in | FM1 + FM2 tags | Operator | Single batch; `RouteMode='Hybrid'`; **no `SpoolProcessing` row** | A spool row created for a hybrid run |
| **BR-05** `FM2_S3` is final and non-bypassable | Schedule authoring / validation | Component states | Ops Manager | S3 always Active; S1 and S2 bypassable | An `Active` schedule with S3 bypassed |
| **BR-06** Tag paths are configuration | Any push | `CommonDB.OPCTags` | Engineering/IT | Correctable without redeployment | A hardcoded path |

### 5.2 Material identity and state

| Rule | Trigger | Expected behaviour | Violation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BR-07** One MMS ID per input coil, closed **strictly on consumption** | Check-in / 0 ft remaining | Auto-close of the previous; never closed by an operator | Any operator-initiated close |
| **BR-08** The payoff transition is driven **solely** by consumption reaching 0 ft | Consumption | Marking welded records the weld only; it does not switch bays | A bay switch on the weld action |
| **BR-09** `INFLAT` is set at **check-in**, not staging, and is `FlatWireDB`-local | Acknowledgement | `Rod.Status='INFLAT'`; `coils.coil_status` **unchanged** | A write to the shared status column |
| **BR-10** Carry-forward is on one persistent rod record | Re-presentation of a partial rod | Existing record retrieved by alpha; a **new** run record opens at footage zero; each segment gets its own spool alpha | Creating a second rod record |
| **BR-11** Material left in the mill at a Mode B removal is **scrapped** | Mode B checkout | Does not carry forward with the rod | Carrying it forward |
| **BR-12** `Blocked` is a **derived** bay state | Inspection fail on a staged row | `Status='Staged'` **and** an inspection column `= 'Fail'` | Adding a fourth `Status` value — it would fall outside the filtered bay index and free an occupied bay |
| **BR-13** Only a WIP rejection clears a `BLOCKED` bay | Inspection fail | Rod → `HOLD`; `UnstageKind='WipRejection'` | Clearing via pre-check-out |

### 5.3 Quality

| Rule | Trigger | Expected behaviour | Violation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BR-14** Out-of-spec suspends material and **does not stop the machine** | SPC submission out of spec | Output to SPC-HOLD; production continues | Stopping the line |
| **BR-15** Force-continue is available **at all times** | Any SPC checkpoint | Submit permitted with out-of-spec readings | A blocked submit |
| **BR-16** SPC completion — not SPC pass — gates the stop transaction | Stop transaction | Update enabled once a checkpoint exists | Requiring in-spec readings |
| **BR-17** The SPC stamp is immutable and footage is captured at **open** | Checkpoint open | Operator, footage, timestamp fixed at open | Capturing footage at submit |
| **BR-18** A weld quality **Fail** does not silently block the run | Weld confirm | Event logged, rods linked, flagged for review, optional pause/alert | Blocking the run silently, or discarding the event |
| **BR-19** A confirmed weld or die change is **immutable** | Confirm | Corrections go through a separate audit flow | In-place edit |

### 5.4 Output and packaging

| Rule | Trigger | Expected behaviour | Violation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BR-20** Weight is derived, never weighed during rolling | Any weight | `A(in²) × 12 × ρ` per foot, round-edge correction where applicable | A scale reading during rolling |
| **BR-21** A scale reading may override **at completion**, and both weights persist | Completion | Operator chooses the basis; both weights and the variance stored regardless | Storing only the chosen basis |
| **BR-22** Exactly two coreless coils per skid, counted as **physical** coils | Coil completion | First opens, second closes, label prints, skid moves to packing | Counting shared coil **records** — a welded coil writes several |
| **BR-23** Labels print **only after the transaction commits** | Completion | Commit → print | Printing on a pending transaction, or showing an alpha before commit |
| **BR-24** Part weights are apportioned, never repeated | Multi-rod coil | Sum of parts = coil net weight; skid totals accumulate **once per physical coil** | Repeating the coil weight on each part |
| **BR-25** Each part's genealogy names **its own** source rod | Multi-rod completion | N identities, each against its own rod | A shared primary rod across all parts |

### 5.5 Allocation and sequencing

| Rule | Trigger | Expected behaviour | Violation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BR-26** At most one order in progress per rod payoff station | Order start | Enforced as a **database constraint**, not an application check alone | A second concurrent order on one station |
| **BR-27** A shared rod is last of the outgoing order and first of the incoming | Sequencing | Never a middle position | A middle placement |
| **BR-28** The rod stays mounted across the boundary | Order completion | One check-in; no dismount, no second check-in | Requiring a remount |
| **BR-29** Orders never close automatically | Allocation reached | Notify; the operator marks complete; the overrun between is **persisted, not discarded** | Auto-close, or discarding the overrun |
| **BR-30** Re-planning is additive | Re-plan | Supersede, never modify in place; consumption keeps a snapshot | In-place modification |
| **BR-31** Active allocations **tile the rod** — no gap, no overlap | Allocation | Complete coverage | A gap or an overlap |
| **BR-32** An output coil's parents all come from **one spool** | Completion | Single-spool parentage | Parents from two spools |

### 5.6 Safety and interlock

| Rule | Trigger | Expected behaviour | Violation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **BR-33** ITInhibit is set and cleared **only** automatically | Four stated conditions | Blocks machine run and related transactions; records no rolling data without an active coil | Any operator set or clear |
| **BR-34** The application **never** sends a stop command to the PLC | Checkout, pause | The operator physically stops the line | An application-issued stop |
| **BR-35** Supervisor overrides and mid-run configuration alerts block passive dismissal | Override / mid-run alert | Escape, click-outside and navigation do not dismiss; the line continues on the **previous** PLC values until acknowledged | Dismissal by Escape or click-outside |
| **BR-36** The PIN is never stored and never carried in the payload | Any supervisor override | Validated, not persisted | A PIN in a request body or a column |

## 6. User Roles

**Six roles**, all present as JWT claims on `ClaimTypes.Role` (confirmed 15 Aug 2026).

| Role | Primary surfaces | Authorised actions in this module | Restricted from |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Operator** | DB2A, DB2, DB3, DB5, DB5A, DB6, DB7, DB7b, DB8, DB11, DB12, DC | Staging, check-in, acknowledgement, run events, SPC, roll adjust apply, die change, pause/resume, WIP rejection flag, Mode A/P checkout, coil completion, packing | Reverting a roll override · activating a pass schedule · disposing a Mode B checkout · editing a schedule mid-run beyond a same-size die swap |
| **Supervisor** | DB1, DB10, pending dispositions | Un-punched login override · out-of-sequence staging authorisation · welded pre-check-out · weight-variance override · **Mode B disposition (Accept/Hold/Reject)** · WIP Suspend review | Pass schedule activation |
| **Operations Manager** | DB9, DB9A | Everything Supervisor does, **plus** schedule create/edit/activate and **roll-override revert** (`FR-212`) | — |
| **Engineering / Maintenance** | DB9, DM | Schedule create/edit/generate · die registration, counter reset, threshold edit, retirement · recording-cadence configuration | Schedule **activation** (Ops Manager) |
| **QA** | SPC-HOLD queue, WIP Held queue | Disposition of held material — **release with concession** or **quarantine/scrap** | Production transactions |
| **Admin** | Platform | User/role provisioning, configuration, reference data | **Deliberately owns no production transaction** |

**Role conflicts and self-approval — a test responsibility:**

- **Can one badge both request and approve?** No requirement forbids an operator who also holds the
  Supervisor claim from authorising their own out-of-sequence staging (`FR-045`), welded pre-check-out
  (`FR-052a`) or Mode B checkout (`FR-323`). **Self-approval is unaddressed** — planned as `SC-159`.
- **Operations Manager and Supervisor are distinct roles** and *"frequently the same person in a small
  crew"* — so a self-approval path is realistic, not theoretical.

> ⛔ **`D-52`: MVP-1 authenticates and does not authorise.** No role policy is registered; **any
> authenticated caller reaches any endpoint this service exposes and nothing can return a `403`.** The
> table above is *what will be enforced*, not *what is enforced*. Every role-boundary scenario in §15 is
> therefore marked **`[MVP-2 enforcement]`** and is planned as **client-side and advisory** for MVP-1,
> with one negative scenario (`SC-158`) asserting the condition explicitly.

## 7. User Journeys

### 7.1 Primary Journeys

| ID | Journey | Route | Steps | Requirements | Ends at |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **UJ-01** | **Rod to intermediate spool** | FL1 | Stage rod on an idle bay → inspect → check in (6-step wizard) → acknowledge schedule → PLC push → run → monitor trace → SPC → spool reaches target → PLC stop → confirm completion → spool alpha → label | `FR-030`–`FR-054`, `FR-060`–`FR-084`, `FR-100`–`FR-120`, `FR-130`–`FR-157`, `FR-180`–`FR-197`, `FR-270`–`FR-277` | An `SP-#####` alpha with a high-temperature label |
| **UJ-02** | **Spool to finished coil** | FL2 | Spool appears in DB5A queue → select/scan → order resolves → DB5 check-in → review source traceability and historical profile → acknowledge FM2 schedule → PLC push → run → final SPC → complete coil → `FW-#####-C##` → skid slot 1 or 2 → label | `FR-090`–`FR-099`, `FR-100`–`FR-120`, `FR-330`–`FR-340`, `FR-345`–`FR-352` | A finished coil on a skid, in the packing queue |
| **UJ-03** | **Rod to finished coil, continuous** | FL3 | Check in at FL1 choosing *"FL1 and FL2 Together"* → station becomes FL3 → **one** acknowledgement pushes FM1 **and** FM2 → run → no intermediate spool, no spool alpha → complete coil | `FR-060`, `FR-061`, `FR-083`, `FR-100`–`FR-120`, `FR-330`–`FR-340` | A finished coil with **no** `SpoolProcessing` row |
| **UJ-04** | **Continuous feed across a weld** | FL1/FL3 | Rod A running → stage rod B on the idle bay → *Mark as welded* (alloy/temper/diameter validated) → weld event recorded → rod A consumed to 0 ft → **payoff transition fires on consumption** → rod B active → weld marker on the trace | `FR-050`, `FR-050a`, `FR-051`, `FR-160`–`FR-172`, `FR-104` | Two rods, one continuous spool, one weld genealogy chain |
| **UJ-05** | **Order handoff on a mounted rod** | FL1/FL3 | Order O1 consuming → allocated weight reached → durable notification → operator marks O1 complete → **O2 begins on the same mount** → overrun between crossing and acknowledgement persisted | `FR-541`–`FR-560` | Two orders, one check-in, one run |
| **UJ-06** | **Coil pair to skid** | FL2/FL3 → packing | Coil 1 completes → skid opens → coil 2 completes → skid closes → skid label prints → staging location assigned → both coil labels confirmed | `FR-335`, `FR-339`, `FR-345`–`FR-352`, `FR-515` | A closed skid with exactly two physical coils |
| **UJ-07** | **Floor supervision** | all | DB1 shows three lines live → alert raised by a rule → supervisor acknowledges → acknowledged count increments | `FR-420`–`FR-428` | A visible, acknowledged floor state |

### 7.2 Alternate Journeys

| ID | Journey | Divergence point | Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| **UJ-08** | **Partial re-check-in (carry-forward)** | A returned rod with `footageRunToDate > 0` is staged: prior-run history shown, **fresh-start control absent from the DOM**, physical-identity confirmation required, a **new** run opens at footage zero | `FR-043`, `[EX §4.7]` |
| **UJ-09** | **Non-recommended schedule** | The operator selects a schedule other than the recommendation: free-text reason captured, selection flagged for Operations review | `FR-071` |
| **UJ-10** | **Direct check-in without pre-check-in** | The rod is scanned straight at DB2: the payoff selector remains editable rather than pre-filled read-only | `FR-082` |
| **UJ-11** | **Out-of-sequence staging** | ⛔ **Undefined.** `FR-045` authorises with a supervisor; `FR-546` refuses. **No alternate journey can be described** — see `CL-03` | `FR-045`, `FR-546` |
| **UJ-12** | **Die change mid-run** | Pause → DC dialog → block selector → scan incoming die → reason code. **Gauge drift / Size change** routes to SPC and blocks full production; **Planned life / Die failure** returns to DB3 | `FR-220`–`FR-234` |
| **UJ-13** | **Roll adjust mid-run** | Measured gauge and width entered → deltas computed → reason chip → Apply → **PLC tag updated immediately** → measurements written as a `RollAdjustTrigger` SPC checkpoint | `FR-200`–`FR-212` |
| **UJ-14** | **Manual spool completion** | The operator declines the PLC-confirmed prompt, then completes manually while weight ≥ target and the line is not running | `FR-147`, `FR-150` |
| **UJ-15** | **Scale-weight override at completion** | Gross scale weight entered → net derived → variance shown in lb and % → operator chooses the basis → both weights persisted | `FR-151`–`FR-156` |
| **UJ-16** | **FL2 pre-check-in (validate the next spool)** | Spool validated and queued before the line needs it; **does not gate check-in** | `FR-533`–`FR-540` ⚠ all `[PROPOSED]`, `Q41` open |
| **UJ-17** | **Camber measurement** | A customer with camber specifications: the field is available, not mandatory | `FR-197` |

### 7.3 Failure Journeys

| ID | Journey | Trigger | Expected behaviour | Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **UJ-18** | **Staging inspection fail** | Any of three items marked Fail | **Hard block, no bypass.** Bay → `BLOCKED`. Only forward action is WIP Rejection, which sets the rod to `HOLD` and unstages with `UnstageKind='WipRejection'` | `FR-041`, `FR-053a` |
| **UJ-19** | **PLC tag write fails mid-batch** | One tag in the batch fails | Exception → **compensating re-clear** of tags already written → shared-schema changes reverted → check-in aborted | `FR-074` ⛔ **untestable through the current interface** — `G58` |
| **UJ-20** | **Network drop during a run** | Transport loss | Cached last-known state renders **within one frame** with a "Reconnecting…" banner — **never a blank screen** — backoff reconnect, automatic line-group re-join | `FR-119`, `NFR006` |
| **UJ-21** | **Mid-run rod removal (Mode B)** | Equipment failure, quality hold, order quantity reached, shift deferral | Pause → resume outcome `CheckOutRod` → footage locked at dialog open → **supervisor approval required** → Pending Disposition, material locked with **no alpha** → Accept / Hold / Reject | `FR-320`–`FR-327` |
| **UJ-22** | **Out-of-spec reading in run** | SPC submission out of spec | Material to **SPC-HOLD**; **the machine keeps producing**; QA dispositions release-with-concession or quarantine/scrap | `FR-187`–`FR-189` |
| **UJ-23** | **Weld quality Fail** | Fail selected with a reason | Event **still logged**, rods linked, flagged for supervisor review, optional pause/alert — **the run is not silently blocked**; the event is immutable | `FR-167`, `FR-168` |
| **UJ-24** | **Spool closes below target** | Stop with weight < target | Treated as an **unplanned stop** on the mill 10-90 pattern. Inside the customer range → continue; outside → supervisor override + hold, **or** a concession offer. **The spool is run off either way** | `FR-130b`, `FR-130c` |
| **UJ-25** | **Mid-run coil break** | Break during a run | Stop **removed and a new stop started from zero** — accumulated weight does **not** resume from the break point | `FR-130d` |
| **UJ-26** | **Checkout attempted while running** | `FL{n}.LineState` reports Running | Blocked, with *"Line is still running. Stop the line before checking out the rod."* The system **never** sends a stop command | `FR-301`, `FR-302` |
| **UJ-27** | **ITInhibit fires** | No rod checked in · no active MMS ID · feet data invalid · ≥2 consecutive recordings missing | Machine run blocked; no rolling data recorded; prominent alert on the recording condition | `FR-008`–`FR-010`, `FR-020` |
| **UJ-28** | **Machine-inspection step fails at check-in** | An OK/NG check marked NG | Rod on hold; **Authorize Override** path capturing supervisor badge, password and a required reason | `FR-081` |
| **UJ-29** | **Wire break** | Break detected | ⛔ **No journey can be described.** Three `Must` requirements with no screen, no table and no phase owner | `FR-280`–`FR-282` |
| **UJ-30** | **Welded rod removed before running** | Pre-check-out of a welded rod | **Supervisor override** — badge + PIN + documented reason — and the rod is set to **`HOLD`**. Removing a welded rod means cutting the material, so it is a rejection, not a return | `FR-052a` |

### 7.4 Critical Paths

Ranked by consequence of failure, not by frequency.

| Rank | Path | Why it is critical | Coverage depth |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Acknowledgement → PLC tag push → machine configured** | The only write path to the machine. A wrong push produces wrong product at line speed under a correct-looking certificate | Full: positive, negative, boundary, partial-failure, per-route, audit |
| **2** | **Weld genealogy → certificate** | **Contractual.** A wrong chain is a wrong certificate to a welding-wire customer | Full, on a **multi-rod, multi-coil** run — a single-rod run does not exercise it |
| **3** | **Footage → weight** | Every weight, yield, cost, remaining-weight and milestone figure. The error would be **self-consistent and hard to spot** | Full, with the worked figure as a regression assertion |
| **4** | **ITInhibit** | The safety interlock, and it must be **line-scoped** — a blocked line must not block the other two | All set conditions + line isolation |
| **5** | **The cross-system check-in boundary** | Not one ACID transaction; recovery undecided. Partial failure leaves a rod checked in with an unconfigured machine, or a configured machine with no record | Full failure-injection |
| **6** | **MMS ID lifecycle** | Closes strictly on consumption; ITInhibit depends on it. A gap between close and re-open inhibits a healthy line | Continuity across the weld transition |
| **7** | **FL2's live gauge/width at 4 s** | ✅ **UNBLOCKED 9 Sep 2026** — `G120` resolved, `A3` retired, `FR-120` superseded: FL2 broadcasts both channels. ⚠ **The risk moved rather than disappearing** — it is now **cadence**: a 4 s stream batched like a 10 Hz one, footage gaps interpolated into a smooth in-spec line, or FL1's consecutive-out-of-spec threshold inherited on FL2 where each reading is 4 s of production | **Testable** |
| **8** | **Skid pairing** | Two coils per skid, counted in **physical** coils — a welded coil writes several shared records and would trip the third-coil refusal on its own second record | Boundary: 1, 2, 3 coils; single-rod and multi-rod |
| **9** | **SPC gating** | Four gates depend on it: check-in, stop transaction, die-change resume, spool alpha issue | All four gates, plus force-continue |
| **10** | **Rod ↔ order handoff** | One run spans two orders; anything reading `FlatWireRun.OrderId` as *"the order this run produced"* is silently wrong | Boundary crossing, overrun, latch-twice |

## 8. Risk Analysis

| Risk ID | Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Risk Level | Test Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R-01** | A wrong or partial pass-schedule push configures the machine incorrectly | Scrap at production volume; wrong product shipped under a correct certificate | Medium | **Critical** | `SC-020`–`SC-035`. Failure injection on every tag in the batch; per-route (FL1/FL2/FL3); assert records-before-push ordering; assert the compensating re-clear. ⛔ **Partial** — `G58` means the trigger is not observable through `OPCConnection`; test at the service boundary with a stubbed writer and record the gap |
| **R-02** | The welding-wire certificate cannot be produced, or is produced wrong | **Contractual failure** | High | **Critical** | `SC-060`–`SC-070`. Reconstruct the full chain on a **two-rod, two-coil** run; assert footage-range coverage and non-overlap; assert per-part weights sum to net. ⛔ **Partial** — the supplier-heat hop has no source (`OI-117`) and the label render is blocked (`Q87`) |
| **R-03** | Every derived weight is wrong by a consistent factor | Yield, cost, consumption, milestones and customer weights all move together — self-consistent and hard to detect | Medium | **Critical** | `SC-071`–`SC-080`. Pin the worked reference (1100, 0.110 × 0.625 → 0.0809 lb/ft) as a regression assertion; assert `0.069` is never produced; assert the basis and factor are persisted per consumption record |
| **R-04** | MVP-1 ships unable to check a rod in, because pass-schedule authoring is MVP-2 and nothing populates the tables | The core operator journey is undeliverable | High | **Critical** | ⛔ **Not a test response — a clarification.** `CL-01`. Until answered, every check-in scenario runs on a **seeded** schedule and the seed dependency is stated in `SC-020`'s precondition |
| **R-05** | 69 `Must` requirements built from unreviewed `[PROPOSED]` text are rejected at UAT | Late rework in the three most structurally coupled areas | High | **Critical** | Scenarios for §5.25–§5.30 are planned and marked **`[PROPOSED]`**, so a rejected requirement invalidates a known, listed set rather than an unknown one |
| **R-06** | Cross-system check-in fails partway with no recovery path | A rod checked in with an unconfigured machine, or a configured machine with no record | Medium | **High** | `SC-036`–`SC-042`. Inject failure at each of the four boundaries: `FlatWireDB`, shared schema, PLC, and the compensating write itself |
| **R-07** | The client believes authorisation is delivered when it is not | A supervisor-approval control anyone can operate, presented as a control | High | **High** | `SC-158` asserts the condition explicitly — **no `403` is reachable** — so the gap is demonstrated, not assumed. `SC-159` covers self-approval |
| **R-08** | Alerts and pending approvals are lost on restart or when nobody is connected | Material locked with no alpha, nobody notified; unauditable acknowledgements | High | **High** | `SC-100`–`SC-104` (alerts), `SC-115`–`SC-118` (Mode B approval). Restart mid-alert; submit with **no supervisor connected** |
| **R-09** | Rod tolerance is seeded at the wrong grain | A validation that silently passes or fails the wrong rods, at the **first** gate in the process | High | **High** | ⛔ **Coverage blocked.** `SC-011`, `SC-012` are **Not Testable** until `CL-05` resolves the grain. Seeding per-alloy would make the tests pass against wrong data |
| **R-10** | FL2 is built to the wrong real-time model | The FL2 dashboard, weight derivation and trace all branch on it | Medium | **High** | ⛔ **Coverage blocked.** `SC-050`, `SC-051` are **Partial** pending `CL-04`. Test both readings as a decision table; commit to neither |
| **R-11** | Requirement coverage cannot be proven at UAT | The release gate asserts coverage that cannot be demonstrated | High | **High** | §17 maps **every** requirement cluster including uncovered ones; §18 reports Not Covered and Not Testable counts explicitly rather than netting them out |
| **R-12** | The skid rule ships in two states (`[CONFIRMED]` vs `[PROPOSED]` counting basis) | A welded coil trips the third-coil refusal on its own second record | Medium | **High** | `SC-090`–`SC-094`. Boundary on 1/2/3 physical coils **and** on a multi-rod coil writing N shared records |
| **R-13** | A gap between MMS close and re-open inhibits a healthy line | Production stops on a correct weld | Medium | **High** | `SC-014`–`SC-016`. Assert ITInhibit does **not** set across a normal weld transition |
| **R-14** | Unbounded lists degrade the always-visible touch panel | The board is *"intended to remain always visible"* and is the first thing that will slow | Medium | **Medium** | `SC-150`–`SC-153`. Volume tests on DB5A, DB9A and DB1. ⛔ **No pass criteria** — the four NFR targets are undefined (`CL-13`) |
| **R-15** | Gloved double-taps duplicate transactions | Duplicate welds, checkpoints, roll adjusts, completions | High | **Medium** | `SC-154`–`SC-157`. Double-submit every confirm. ⚠ Only `FR-549` states a duplication rule, and only for a rod scan — the expected result elsewhere is **underived** |
| **R-16** | The simulator becomes the de facto specification of machine behaviour | The system passes every test and fails at commissioning | High | **Medium** | Commissioning checklist, not a scenario. `[SIM §5.6]`'s ten assumptions each need a named confirming act on the real line |
| **R-17** | Shift boundaries corrupt run and utilisation data | Daily occurrence | Medium | **Medium** | `SC-160`–`SC-162`. ⚠ Expected results **underived** — no shift-boundary rule exists (`CL-29`) |
| **R-18** | Two operators on one line collide | Duplicate or conflicting transactions | Medium | **Medium** | `SC-163`, `SC-164`. ⚠ Expected results **underived** — arbitration is unspecified outside the stop popup |
| **R-19** | SPC-HOLD cannot be persisted, so held material is not actually held | Out-of-spec material advances, ships or is released | High | **High** | ⛔ **Not Testable** until `OI-23` gives SPC-HOLD a column. `SC-081` records the block |
| **R-20** | `Rework` is selectable and unpersistable | One of three dispositions fails at the database | High | **High** | ⛔ **Not Testable** until `OI-22`. `SC-110` records the block |

## 9. Test Coverage Strategy

### 9.1 The principle

**Coverage depth follows consequence, not requirement count.** Roughly 40 requirements sit on paths where
a defect produces wrong physical product or a wrong contractual document; they receive positive, negative,
boundary, failure, concurrency, persistence and audit coverage. Roughly 200 sit on operator-facing paths
where a defect produces a wrong screen; they receive positive, negative and the primary error path.
Roughly 75 are MVP-2 and are planned but not scheduled.

### 9.2 Depth tiers

| Tier | Areas | Dimensions applied |
|---|---|---|
| **P0 — full depth** | Pass-schedule acknowledgement → PLC push · weld genealogy → certificate · footage → weight · ITInhibit · cross-system check-in boundary · MMS ID lifecycle · skid pairing | Positive · negative · boundary · **failure injection** · per-route · persistence · audit · concurrency · regression |
| **P1 — deep** | Check-in gates · the three checkout modes · carry-forward · SPC gating · roll adjust · die change · pause/resume · WIP rejection · alert rules · reconnect · run-end and check-in write-backs · rod↔order handoff | Positive · negative · boundary · state transition · persistence · audit |
| **P2 — standard** | Pre-check-in queue and bay states · spool queue · active-run presentation · packing station · stop transaction · traveler sections | Positive · negative · primary error |
| **P3 — shallow** | Shift summary · OEE · reports · Die Management · Pass Schedule List | Happy path + primary error. **Descope-ladder candidates** |

### 9.3 Coverage dimensions and where each is justified

| Dimension | Applied to | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| **Positive** | All in-scope requirements | Baseline |
| **Negative** | Every gate, every validation, every enumerated reason list | The register is gate-heavy; a gate untested for its negative case is untested |
| **Boundary** | Tolerance bands (asymmetric), payoff weight thresholds (3,000 / 2,000 lb), milestone percentages (75/90/100), die life bands, skid counts (1/2/3), footage 0 vs > 0, aspect ratio 5.5, Rod Buildup ≤ 40, variance ±2 % | Every one of these is a stated number with behaviour on each side |
| **Equivalence partitioning** | Material statuses, run statuses, component states (`Active`/`Bypass`/`Skip`), checkpoint types, reason codes, dispositions | Enumerated vocabularies with distinct downstream behaviour |
| **Decision table** | ITInhibit set conditions (4 inputs) · resume outcomes (4) · checkout mode selection (checked-in × footage × welded) · die-change reason → routing · disposition → status transition · FL2 live-vs-null (**both branches, pending `CL-04`**) | Combinations where the outcome is not a simple function of one input |
| **State transition** | Rod material status · run status · staging status · bay states · pass schedule status · spool status · skid open/closed | Seven documented state machines with illegal transitions worth asserting |
| **Role / permission** | Every restricted action | ⚠ **MVP-1: client-side only.** Server enforcement is MVP-2 (`D-52`) |
| **Data integrity** | Every persisted transaction: computed columns, defaults, constraints, referential integrity, footage-range non-overlap, weight apportionment | The register places heavy trust in database constraints (`FR-543` requires one explicitly) |
| **Integration** | PLC push/clear · OPC reads · SignalR · four shared databases · `united_db..alloys` · label printers | Five external boundaries, each with its own failure modes |
| **Failure / recovery** | Partial PLC batch · cross-database partial commit · transport loss · reconnect · retry idempotency · compensating-write failure | `OI-39` is Critical and undecided; the tests must exist regardless of which model is chosen |
| **Concurrency** | Two lines running independently · two dashboards · two operators on one line · concurrent skid contention · bay-uniqueness race | `NFR007` covers only the first |
| **Security** | Authentication, PIN non-persistence, audit completeness | ⚠ Authorisation deferred; **the absence is asserted** |
| **Regression** | The shared-schema writes, `projects/shared` consumers, existing WIP/reqsum/skid behaviour | See §14 |

### 9.4 What is deliberately **not** covered

| Not covered | Why |
|---|---|
| DB13, DB14, DB3 Machine View | Withdrawn by client decision 4 Aug 2026. **No test cases** |
| Rod receiving, planning, scheduling, Web, Yield/Cost internals, OPC server | Out of scope per `[TS §2.2]`; fixture-supplied |
| Shared-schema rename regression | `D-32` — there is no migration, so there is no regression surface |
| Server-side role enforcement | `D-52` — MVP-1 registers no policy. Covered only as a negative assertion |
| Pass-schedule generation formulas `FR-381`–`FR-387` **as published** | `[MS §10.5]` supersedes all five on the arithmetic. Testing the published formulas would assert known-wrong behaviour |

---

## 10. Test Design Techniques

| Technique | Applicable? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Functional / end-to-end** | **Yes** | Three distinct routes (FL1, FL2, FL3), each producing a different output artefact. `UJ-01`–`UJ-03` are the release-gate journeys |
| **Positive testing** | **Yes** | Baseline for all 424 requirements |
| **Negative testing** | **Yes** | The register is built around gates with explicitly stated bypass rules. A no-bypass gate needs the negative case to prove no control exists — `FR-043` requires **absence from the DOM**, which only a negative test can assert |
| **Validation / error handling** | **Yes** | Every group states an *Error paths* line with specific status codes (`409`, `422`, `404`, `500`) |
| **Boundary-value analysis** | **Yes** | Numerous stated numeric boundaries with distinct behaviour either side: 3,000 / 2,000 lb payoff, 75/90/100 % milestones, ±2 % variance, 60/85 % and 65/80 % die life, 0 vs > 0 footage, aspect ratio 5.5, 40 Rod Buildup, 2-coils-per-skid, 50 % then every 10 % buildup. ⚠ **Rod-diameter bands cannot be partitioned** — the values exist but at a grain the table cannot hold (`CL-05`) |
| **Equivalence partitioning** | **Yes** | Enumerated vocabularies with distinct downstream behaviour — 7 material statuses, 4 run statuses, 3 component states, 5 checkpoint types, 5 die-change reasons, 5 WIP rejection groups, 3 dispositions, 6 line states |
| **Decision tables** | **Yes** | Several outcomes depend on input combinations, not single inputs: ITInhibit (4 conditions → 1 output), checkout mode (checked-in × footage × welded → 4 modes), die-change reason → routing + SPC requirement, resume outcome → 4 distinct state effects, weight basis (scale entered × variance × override complete) |
| **State-transition testing** | **Yes** | Seven documented state machines with named legal transitions. Illegal transitions are worth asserting because `[BR §3.4]` warns that adding a state value would fall outside a filtered index and free an occupied bay |
| **Pairwise / combinatorial** | **Yes, narrowly** | Route (3) × schedule state (3) × edge type (2) × component bypass patterns produces a large space. Pairwise is justified for **pass-schedule validation only**; elsewhere the combinations are small enough to enumerate |
| **Role / permission testing** | **Partial** | The matrix exists and is `[MVP-2 enforcement]`. Client-side gating (`FR-212`) is testable now; server enforcement is not — nothing can return a `403` |
| **Business-rule testing** | **Yes** | 36 rules extracted in §5, each with a stated violation |
| **Data-integrity / database validation** | **Yes** | See §12. The register explicitly delegates a rule to the database (`FR-543`) and relies on computed columns, filtered unique indexes and a non-overlap trigger |
| **Integration testing** | **Yes** | Five external boundaries. ⚠ **The API integration test level was withdrawn on 15 Aug 2026 and `D-50` reinstated only the .NET unit level** — so integration coverage must come from E2E and contract-by-inspection, and this plan says so rather than assuming a suite exists |
| **Failure / recovery testing** | **Yes** | `OI-39` (Critical) makes recovery the single most under-specified area on the critical path |
| **Duplicate-submission testing** | **Yes** | Gloved operation on a touch panel is a stated operating condition. Only one requirement addresses duplication |
| **Security testing** | **Partial** | Authentication, PIN non-persistence and audit completeness are testable. **Authorisation is not** — `D-52` |
| **Performance / load** | **Partial** | A hub load test is scheduled at QA2. ⛔ **It has no pass criteria and therefore cannot fail** — four NFR targets are undefined |
| **Accessibility** | **Partial** | 14 px minimum text, ≥ 48 px tap targets and *no action may depend on hover* are testable. Screen-reader and contrast requirements are not stated |
| **Compatibility** | **No** | A single target: Chromium on a 1920 × 1080 touch panel. No matrix to cover |
| **Localisation** | **No** | No localisation requirement exists |
| **Regression** | **Yes** | Based on actual change impact — see §14 |
| **Exploratory** | **Yes** | Justified specifically for the 6 unimplementable and 15 contradictory requirements: scripted cases cannot express an undefined outcome, but a timeboxed session can characterise what the build actually does |

## 11. Test Data Requirements

**Categories, not values.** Where a value is stated in the sources it is named; where it is not, the
category records what must be supplied and by whom.

### 11.1 Reference data

| Category | Content needed | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Stands** | FM1 (12″), FM2_S1 (8″), FM2_S2 (6″), FM2_S3 (6″, final, non-bypassable) | Seeded, fixed IDENTITY | ✅ Available |
| **Drawers** | DB1, DB2 | Seeded | ✅ Available |
| **Die inventory** | Per-tool dies with size, type, condition, life threshold, accumulated footage | `ToolingInventoryDie`, Phase 1 | ✅ Available |
| **Alloy properties** | Max reduction per pass, springback, gauge/width tolerance defaults, speed range for 1100, 1350, 3003, 5052, 6061 | Process Engineering sign-off | ⚠ **Unsigned.** Duplicates `united_db..alloys` (`OI-93`) |
| **Rod diameter tolerance bands** | Min/max for gauge, width, diameter, ovality — **asymmetric permitted** | Client | ⛔ **Values arrived at the wrong grain** — per vendor and per size band (`CL-05`) |
| **Published SPC tolerance bands** | Per alloy and temper | QA / Process Engineering | ⛔ **Undefined** (`OI-57`). SPC control limits cannot be configured |
| **Scrap boxes** | Alloy-keyed, `SB-{alloy}-{nn}` | External (slitter source) | ⚠ `OI-15` |
| **Spool article registry** | `SP-0001`…`SP-0045` (44 active + 1 withdrawn), **four digits deliberately** | Seeded | ✅ Available. ⛔ **Do not "correct" to five digits** — it would collide with `SpoolProcessing.Alpha` |
| **Pass schedules** | ≥ 10 covering Draft/Active/Inactive, FL1/FL2/FL3, Round/Square, with component sets | Seeded | ✅ Available. ⚠ Header comment claims 3/7 standalone/hybrid; actual is 4/6 |
| **Shift schedules** | For auto shift-based login and utilisation windows | Not stated | ⛔ **Not specified anywhere** |
| **Customer order weight ranges** | Min/max spool weight per order | Planning / Web | ⛔ **Which order field carries it is open** (`CL-24`) |
| **Weld joint limit** | Max joints per finished coil | Sales / Contracts | ⛔ **TBD**, and no field exists (`CL-20`) |

### 11.2 Material data

| Category | Content needed | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Rods — clean** | `R#####` in `coils` with a `planning_routings` allocation, valid alloy/temper/diameter/weight | Canonical: `R00041`–`R00043` |
| **Rods — refusal cases** | No allocation · status `COMPLETE`/`HOLD`/`SCRAP` · already `INFLAT` · already staged elsewhere · not in `coils` at all | One per refusal limb of `FR-044` and `FR-532` |
| **Rods — partial** | `FootageRunToDate > 0` with a prior run reference and prior spool alphas | Drives the carry-forward gate |
| **Rods — multi-order** | One rod allocated to two orders, pinned-last on O1 and pinned-first on O2 | Required by `UJ-05`; **the case `FR-044` currently refuses** |
| **Rods — boundary diameter** | At the band minimum, maximum, and just outside each | ⛔ Blocked on `CL-05` |
| **Rods — ovality** | M1 ≠ M2 producing ovality at, inside and outside tolerance | `FR-069` |
| **Spools — runnable** | `RECEIVED`, `STAGED` with a source FL1 run and source rod alphas | `FR-099` |
| **Spools — non-runnable** | `HOLD`, `INFLAT`, `COMPLETE`, `SCRAP` | Each must list without a check-in action |
| **Spools — unallocated** | `OrderNo` null | **A valid single-spool result, not an error** |
| **Spools — hybrid-origin** | Produced under a `Hybrid` route mode | Must be marked; `OI-47` |
| **Spools — multi-rod** | Wound from two or more source rods with a weld between | **Required for BO2.** ⚠ `G42`: `SpoolProcessing` cannot represent multi-rod genealogy |
| **Coils — single-rod** | One source rod, one part identity, one shared record | `FR-566` |
| **Coils — multi-rod** | Two source rods, two part identities, apportioned weights | `FR-561`–`FR-567`. ⛔ `G54`: the mint precondition is unbuilt |

### 11.3 Transactional and state data

| Category | Content needed |
|---|---|
| **Runs** | Running · Paused (with an open `RunPauseEvent`) · Complete · Aborted (with a mid-run checkout producing a partial spool) |
| **Bay states** | `NOT STAGED` · `PRE-CHECKED-IN` · `ACTIVE` · `BLOCKED` (staged **with** an inspection Fail — the derived state) |
| **Weld events** | Pass and Fail, each with the required fail reason; a chain of ≥ 2 welds on one spool |
| **SPC checkpoints** | One per type; in-spec and out-of-spec; **asymmetric tolerance** cases (to expose `G51`) |
| **Pending dispositions** | Mode B submissions awaiting Accept / Hold / Reject, including one submitted with **no supervisor connected** |
| **Skids** | Open with one coil · closed with two · an attempt at a third · a skid holding a multi-rod coil |
| **Alerts** | One of each of the five rules, active and acknowledged, **surviving a restart** ⛔ no store exists |
| **Allocations** | Tiled with no gap or overlap · a gap case · an overlap case · a superseded allocation · a substitution with no planned allocation |

### 11.4 Real-time and PLC data

| Category | Content needed | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Gauge/width streams** | In spec · out of spec · N consecutive out-of-spec · missing readings (1, then ≥ 2 consecutive) | ⚠ N is undefined (`CL-22`) |
| **Line state transitions** | `RUNNING → STOPPED` edges, jogs shorter than the dwell, thread mode, fault | ⛔ **The vocabulary is undocumented** (`CL-27`) |
| **Footage counter** | Monotonic increment; frozen at pause; locked at dialog open | |
| **Payoff weights** | Crossing 3,000 lb and 2,000 lb; a **zero reading on an occupied bay** (to prove `FR-424`) | |
| **Tag write outcomes** | Success; single-tag failure; whole-batch failure; failure of the compensating re-clear | ⛔ **Not expressible through `OPCConnection`** (`G58`) |
| **Cadence** | 4 ft and 20 ft, and a non-default configured value applied without a restart | `NFR003`, `NFR004` |

### 11.5 Test-data constraints

- **Seed order is strict** — Lookup → Schedule → Materials → Runs → Quality/Output — because the schedule seed depends on lookup IDENTITY values.
- **`CoilTraceability` ranges must be seeded non-overlapping** or the trigger rejects them.
- **Computed columns and `ROWVERSION` are never inserted.**
- **Every block is guarded by `IF NOT EXISTS`**, so `RunAll` is idempotent.
- ⚠ **Known seed defect:** the `WipRejection` seed violates `FK_WipRejection_Reason` and **has been failing silently** (`G108`). Any WIP-rejection scenario must verify its fixture actually inserted.
- ⚠ **`DieHistory` is seeded nowhere**, yet the seed records the die change that would write it (`G115`).
- ⚠ **`SpoolOrder` is written by nothing** (`G109`) — fixtures must create it directly.

---

## 12. Database Validation Requirements

**Stated as validation needs, not as physical schema.** Where the register names a specific mechanism the
name is carried; no table, column or query is invented.

### 12.1 Persistence — what must be provable after each transaction

| Transaction | Must persist | Named issue |
|---|---|---|
| **Staging** | Staging row at `Staged`, server-assigned sequence, snapshot planned sequence, override flag + supervisor + timestamp + reason, WIP queue compensating write, **`coils.coil_status` unchanged** | `OI-01` — whether the reqsum insert stays at staging is open |
| **Check-in** | Run header, check-in record, pre-run SPC checkpoint + measurements, staging row consumed with the link back, `Rod.Status='INFLAT'`, tag-push outcome flag, per-write audit | ⛔ **The per-write PLC audit has no named sink** (`OI-126`) |
| **Check-in write-back** | Routing copy, order reference, reqsum entry, actual start date **only when not already started**, WIP station claim, station stamp **without altering status**, one transaction-log entry — **all in one transaction** | `FR-526`; `Q37`–`Q40` unsigned |
| **Weld** | Both alphas, both payoff positions, footage, type, quality, operator, **server-side timestamp**; active-rod pointer advanced; weld-pending cleared | `OI-127` — encoder read and material boundary are different moments |
| **SPC checkpoint** | Type, operator, footage **captured at open**, timestamp, measurements, observation; the stamp immutable | `G51` — `InSpec` is wrong for asymmetric tolerances |
| **Roll adjust** | One row **per changed gap** with component, old, new, delta, reason, operator, timestamp, footage; a linked `RollAdjustTrigger` checkpoint | `OI-32` — no revert endpoint |
| **Die change** | Block, both alphas and sizes, condition, reason, footage, output alpha, operator, timestamp, quality hold, SPC-required flag, auto-created linked roll override | `OI-18` — the checkpoint cannot join back |
| **Pause / resume** | Reason **code and category** (not a label), notes mandatory on `Other`, frozen footage, outcome, elapsed duration | `G83` — four reason codes lost their vocabulary |
| **WIP rejection** | Alpha, stage, footage, measured value, target range, deviation, observation, operator, disposition, new status; link to the trace position | ⛔ **`Rework` has no status value and no return-stage column** (`OI-22`) |
| **Rod checkout** | Alpha, payoff, originating check-in link, mode, reason, locked footage, remaining weight, rod and material disposition, operator, timestamp, notes; supervisor decision for Mode B | `G7` — no durable approval queue |
| **Coil completion** | Coil alpha, order link, dimensions, both weights and the variance **regardless of chosen basis**, schedule ID + version + **configuration snapshot**, traceability rows, skid link | `OI-24` — lot number has no column |
| **Run-end write-back** | Per source rod: shared coil identity, coil row, order link, cost record, cut record, WIP transaction — **all or nothing**, retry writing only unrecorded parts | `G54` — the mint precondition is unbuilt |

### 12.2 Constraint and integrity validation

| Validation | What must be asserted | Named issue |
|---|---|---|
| **Bay uniqueness** | One rod per payoff bay, enforced by the filtered unique index — **not by read-then-write** | ⛔ `G21` — the index does not enforce it across FL1/FL3 |
| **One order per payoff station** | Enforced as a **database constraint**, not an application check | `FR-543` |
| **Footage-range non-overlap** | Traceability ranges cover the coil with no gap and no overlap | Trigger-enforced; assert both directions |
| **Allocation tiling** | Active allocations tile the rod with no gap and no overlap | `FR-557` |
| **Part-weight apportionment** | Sum of part weights = coil net weight; skid totals accumulate **once per physical coil** | `FR-567` |
| **Identity exclusion** | No identity appears in both spool-segment and coil-part records | ⚠ **Not expressible as a constraint** — `FR-561d` says so. **Assert by test** |
| **Segment parentage** | A coil part naming a segment resolves to a segment on the same rod | ⚠ **No FK can enforce this** — `FR-561e`. **Assert by test** |
| **Enum mirroring** | C# ↔ TypeScript ↔ database `CHECK` agree for all enumerated vocabularies | ⚠ `G56` — the three-way diff cannot be run for two of fourteen enums |
| **Referential integrity** | Every FK holds under the seed and under teardown | ⚠ `G111` — 13 of 69 FKs have an unindexed child column |
| **Component state** | Three-value (`Active`/`Bypass`/`Skip`), never boolean; `FM2_S3` never bypassed in an `Active` schedule | `G41` — `CK_PSC_FM1NotBypassable` is line-blind, so a correct FL2 schedule cannot be authored |
| **Computed columns** | Never inserted; recomputed correctly for asymmetric tolerances | ⛔ `G51` |

### 12.3 Cross-database validation

| Validation | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Check-in spans `FlatWireDB` and the shared schema in **one `SqlTransaction`** under the local transaction manager, **with no MSDTC** | `FR-526`, `[INT §8.0]`, `[ARC §10]` |
| ⛔ **Must be validated on the shared instance `DEV00164-001`, never LocalDB** | LocalDB has no `united_db`, so a build validated only there **silently loses atomicity** |
| Every shared write lands in a column that **already exists** — no rename, no new column, no new status value | `D-32` |
| `INFLAT` never reaches `coils.coil_status` | `D-32`, `BR-09` |
| ρ resolves from `united_db..alloys.alloy_density` | `FR-137`, `FR-332` |
| Alloy max reduction resolves from `united_db..alloys.Draw_max_reduction`, **not** the local seed | `FR-383`, `OI-93` |

### 12.4 Teardown and idempotency

- `RunAll` is idempotent and safe to re-run against an existing database.
- `FlatWire_DDL_99_Teardown.sql` drops everything and **must never run against production data**.
- ⚠ **SQLCMD mode is required** — `:r` includes resolve **relative to the invocation directory**.

## 13. Integration Testing Requirements

### 13.1 Boundaries

| # | Boundary | Direction | Success mode | Failure modes to exercise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **I-1** | **PLC via `OPCConnection` — write** | Out | One batch per acknowledgement; outcome recorded; per-write audit | Single-tag failure · whole-batch failure · **compensating re-clear failure** · unreachable controller · **FL3's two controllers, one succeeding and one failing** |
| **I-2** | **PLC via OPC — read** | In | Speed, footage, line state, payoff weights at the configured cadence | Stale tag · invalid feet data · ≥ 2 consecutive missing recordings (→ ITInhibit) · a zero weight on an occupied bay |
| **I-3** | **SignalR `FlatWireHub`** | Both | Push at 1 s default; line-group isolation; durable prompts re-delivered on reconnect | Transport loss mid-run · loss during a modal · reconnect and group re-join · **server unable to broadcast while transactions still commit** · two clients on two lines with no cross-talk |
| **I-4** | **Shared databases** (`coils`, `wip_stations`, `planning_routings`, `routings`, reqsum, `wip_coil_orders`) | Both | All-or-nothing with the flat wire records, one transaction | Partial commit · reqsum reversal on an unrun rod · **refusal** of reversal on a rod that has run · station release at run end and at checkout |
| **I-5** | **`united_db..alloys`** | In | ρ and max reduction resolve | Missing alloy row · a null density |
| **I-6** | **`CommonDB.OPCTags`** | In | Tag paths resolve from registration, correctable without redeployment | Missing registration · a line with **no system-error tag row** (`G95` — `GetOPCInfo` returns an empty list) |
| **I-7** | **`Login` / JWT** | In | Six roles present on `ClaimTypes.Role` | No token → `401` · expired token · **a role claim whose coded value does not map** (fails **silent** for SignalR targeting) |
| **I-8** | **Label printers** | Out | Standard Sato and high-temperature per line | Printer offline **after commit** · ⛔ `G78` — the station registry holds **one** printer and the topology needs two |
| **I-9** | **Packing / shipping / certification** | Out | Skid and coil records resolve; certificate chain reconstructs | ⛔ Blocked — `Q87` and `OI-117` |

### 13.2 Cross-cutting integration concerns

| Concern | Requirement | Test response |
|---|---|---|
| **Mapping** | Every pushed value maps to a tag path owned solely by `[PLC]` | Assert no tag path string is constructed outside the tag layer |
| **Ordering** | Records **before** the push, always | Assert on the failure path, not only the success path |
| **Timeout** | Not specified anywhere for the PLC write | ⛔ **Undefined** — record as a gap, do not invent a value |
| **Retry** | Run-end write-back retry writes **only unrecorded parts** and reports **all** of them | Assert idempotency across a retry |
| **Duplicate request** | Only `FR-549` states a rule, and only for a rod scan | Exercise; expected result **underived** elsewhere |
| **Partial failure** | Four boundaries can fail independently within one check-in | Failure injection at each, then assert observable system state |
| **Consistency** | After any partial failure, the run must not be left `Running` with an unconfigured machine | ⚠ **Derived** — the source is silent on the compensating write failing |
| **Availability** | No requirement states behaviour when the PLC is unreachable, as distinct from a write failing | ⛔ **Gap** — `CL-33` |

### 13.3 Environment note that changes what can be integration-tested

> ⛔ **The API integration test level was withdrawn on 15 August 2026 and is NOT reinstated.** `D-50`
> (5 Sep 2026) reversed the withdrawal **for the .NET unit level only** — there is still no xUnit suite
> against a seeded `FlatWireDB`, and the **contract level is manual review**, not an executed suite.
>
> **Consequence for this plan:** integration coverage must be delivered through **E2E on staging with the
> test-only `OPCConnection` double**, plus contract-by-inspection per PR. This plan does not assume an
> integration suite exists, and the Test Design Agent must not design cases for a level that has no
> runner. Where a scenario below is only executable at the integration level, it is marked
> **`[E2E-only]`**.

## 14. Regression Impact

### 14.1 Change impact — what this module actually touches

| Touched | Change | Regression surface | Depth |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Shared `coils`** | **Read and written as it stands; never altered** (`D-32`) | Existing readers of `coils` see new rows of a new kind, and a new `flattening_station` stamp on rod rows | **High.** `Q39` asks whether stamping is safe for existing consumers and **the impact audit that would have answered it was cancelled with `D-32`** |
| **`wip_stations`** | `coilno` claimed at check-in, released at run end and at checkout | The registry is **uniquely indexed** on that column | **High.** `OI-112` — nothing released it until `FR-527` |
| **reqsum / `wip_coil_orders`** | Entry created when the rod is not yet reqsummed; reversed on an unrun removal | Order material status recomputation | **High.** `Q40` — delete the row or leave it, unanswered |
| **`planning_routings` / `routings`** | `actual_start_date` stamped **only when not already started** | Existing start-date consumers | **Medium** |
| **Skid tables** (`wip_skids`, `wip_skid_coils`) | Flat wire opens and closes skids by the existing rules | The slitter skid path shares the mechanism | **High.** The write-back was modelled on `CreateSkid_MoveCutsOnSkid` |
| **Coil alpha generator** | Called against a source rod's alpha, once **per source rod** | The generator sweeps `coils` unqualified; `proddb..coils` is a **synonym** onto `CommonDB..coils` | **High.** `OI-125` resolved the identity question; the sweep is shared |
| **`CommonDB.OPCTags`** | New flat wire registrations | `GetOPCInfo` behaviour for other lines | **Medium.** `G96` — the module-id constant is stale; `5` looks free and is in production |
| **`projects/shared`** | `lib-nav-rail`, `lib-chart-canvas`, `lib-trace-panel`, `buildTraceConfig` | ⚠ **23 dependent libraries.** `NavRailItem` is a deliberate **structural subset** of `shop-floor-common`'s type so `slitter-traveler-landing` passes its array in unmapped — **adding a required field breaks slitter** | **High.** `ng build shared` before any dependent test run |
| **`ua_user` grants** | `db_datareader`/`db_datawriter` on four shared databases | ⚠ `G114` — on databases this project does not own | **Medium.** Security regression |

### 14.2 Explicitly **not** a regression surface

| Not regressed | Why |
|---|---|
| The `FW-001` shared-schema rename | **`D-32` — there is no migration**, so there is no regression surface. Retired 18 Aug 2026 |
| `coils.coil_status` vocabulary | `INFLAT` never enters it; the value is `FlatWireDB`-local |
| OPC server behaviour | Unchanged; only the PLCs are new |
| Existing slitter, mill and furnace transactions | No shared code path is modified — **except `projects/shared`**, which is why that row is High |

### 14.3 Regression triggers

Run the regression set when any of these change: a `projects/shared` control's public surface · the shared
write-back procedures · the coil alpha generator · the skid procedures · the `OPCTags` registration ·
`ua_user` grants · any DDL file (`RunAll` is ordered, and `06` holds all FKs).

⚠ **`OI-111` is not a regression target.** It asks which existing reports read `coils.coil_status` — an
inventory question for IT, not a case in this plan.

## 16. Clarifications Required

**Severity is stated in each row.** Clarifications already carried by the requirement analysis are cited
by their `RA-Q##` id and not renumbered; the `CL-##` here is the planning-side handle.

| ID | Requirement/AC | Issue | Impact | Clarification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **CL-01** | `FR-070`, `RA-Q01` | **Blocker.** DB9/DB9A are MVP-2 and `OI-110` records the pass schedule tables as populated by nobody, yet every MVP-1 check-in requires an `Active` schedule | `SC-020`–`SC-035` and every check-in journey run on a seeded schedule. **Phase 4 cannot be demonstrated end to end without one** | How is an `Active` pass schedule created for MVP-1? |
| **CL-02** | `FR-070`, `RA-Q02`, `OI-46` | **Blocker.** The no-match path at check-in is undefined | `SC-022` has no expected result | When no `Active` schedule matches, does the system block and alert Operations, or permit a credential-gated override? |
| **CL-03** | `FR-045` vs `FR-546`, `RA-Q03` | **Blocker.** `FR-045` authorises an out-of-sequence rod; `FR-546` refuses it. Both `Must`, both at staging and check-in | `SC-048` and `UJ-11` cannot assert an outcome | Is an out-of-sequence rod refused, or authorised by a supervisor? |
| ~~**CL-04**~~ | `FR-101`, `FR-137`, `FR-421`, `G120` | ✅ **CLOSED 9 Sep 2026 — no longer a blocker.** `A3` retired and `FR-120` superseded; FL2 measures live at 4 s. ⭐ The deciding evidence was **internal**: FL3 runs the **same FM2** in real time, and `FW-181` already conceded FL2-within-FL3 has live gauge. ⚠ **`FR-137` did NOT branch on it after all** — the weight basis is **nominal for every line** (`Q10`, `D17`), so the derivation is unchanged | `SC-050`, `SC-051` now **full**. ⚠ Residuals `PLC-Q15` (unit) and `PLC-Q19` (one stand or two) are commissioning items, not test blockers | Does FL2 emit live gauge and width to the dashboard while running? |
| **CL-05** | `FR-042`, `FR-065`, `RA-Q05`, `G121` | **Blocker.** Tolerance values arrived at a per-vendor, per-size-band grain the data model cannot hold | `SC-011`, `SC-012` are Not Testable. Seeding per-alloy would make the tests pass against **wrong** data | At what grain are rod diameter tolerances held? |
| **CL-06** | `FR-336`, `FR-563`, `RA-Q06`, `Q87` | **Blocker.** What a multi-rod coil prints is deferred | `SC-096` has no expected result; a contractual deliverable is unbuildable | What do the coil label and certificate print for a two-rod coil? |
| **CL-07** | `FR-074`, `G58` | **Blocker.** `OPCConnection` returns `200` regardless of outcome, so the failure `FR-074` responds to is not observable | `SC-027`, `SC-028` cannot be executed through the production interface | Will the write interface report failure, or should `FR-074` be re-specified against observable state? |
| **CL-08** | `FR-153`, `RA-Q08` | **Blocker.** ±2 % is arithmetically unreachable from target dimensions | `SC-072` is written to fail deliberately; `FR-559` inherits it | What variance threshold should trigger the override, against which basis? |

## 19. Planning Review

A second pass was made over this plan before saving. Findings are recorded as results, not as intentions.

### 19.1 Checks performed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Every requirement and acceptance criterion analysed** | ✅ All 424 defined requirements appear in §17, grouped into 104 clusters. The 23 referenced-only withdrawn numbers and `FR-512` are accounted for as Not Covered with a reason |
| **Primary journeys covered** | ✅ `UJ-01`–`UJ-07`, each mapped to scenarios |
| **Alternate journeys covered** | ⚠ 9 of 10. `UJ-11` (out-of-sequence staging) **cannot be described** — `CL-03` |
| **Failure journeys covered** | ⚠ 12 of 13. `UJ-29` (wire break) **cannot be described** — `CL-09` |
| **Critical paths covered** | ⚠ **9 of 10 fully** — path 7 (FL2 gauge) **unblocked 9 Sep 2026**, `CL-04` closed. Path 2 (weld genealogy) still terminates in a field with no source (`CL-12`) |
| **State transitions covered** | ✅ All seven documented state machines, including illegal transitions and the derived `BLOCKED` bay state |
| **Important business rules have a test response** | ✅ All 36 rules in §5 map to at least one scenario. 7 map only to a Not Testable scenario, each named |
| **Critical and High risks have a test response** | ✅ All 20 risks in §8. **5 have only a partial response**, each with the blocking clarification named |
| **Positive / negative / boundary / role / data / database / integration / recovery / regression covered where applicable** | ⚠ All present except **role**, which is `[MVP-2 enforcement]` and covered only as a negative assertion (`SC-158`), and **performance**, which has scenarios but **no pass criteria** |
| **Every acceptance criterion is Covered / Partially / Not Covered / Not Testable with a reason** | ✅ §17 |
| **Scenarios are distinct, independent and risk-prioritised** | ✅ Duplicates combined — the SPC/roll-adjust overlap (`FR-210`) is one scenario naming both; the payoff-colour conflict is one scenario naming `FR-034` and `FR-106` |
| **Facts, derived behaviour, assumptions and clarifications separated** | ✅ §4 separates derived behaviour explicitly; assumptions are carried as `RA-ASM##`; all 50 clarifications are in §16 |
| **Missing technical information documented without invented detail** | ✅ No boundary, threshold, endpoint, table, column or role has been invented. Where a value is needed and absent, a clarification is raised instead |

### 19.2 Remaining gaps in this plan

| Gap | Why it remains |
|---|---|
| **No pass criteria for any performance scenario** | Four NFR targets are undefined in every source. Inventing them would make the load test *"cannot fail"* into *"passes against a number we chose"* — worse, not better |
| **Expected results underived for duplicate submission, shift boundary and multi-operator scenarios** | The register states no rule. The scenarios exist so the behaviour is characterised; the expected result must come from `CL-29`, `CL-30` and a duplication rule |
| **Integration-level scenarios have no runner** | The API integration level was withdrawn and not reinstated. Marked `[E2E-only]`; this plan does not assume a suite that does not exist |
| **69 `[PROPOSED]` requirements are planned as though they will be accepted** | The alternative — not planning them — would leave the largest structural area untested. They are marked so a rejection invalidates a **known, listed** set |
| **MVP-2 scenarios are planned, not scheduled** | Scope, not coverage |

### 19.3 Residual risks after planning

1. **`CL-01` is unanswered and it is the largest single risk to demonstrability**, not just to coverage.
   A test plan cannot compensate for a workflow with no way to create its own precondition.
2. **The weld genealogy chain — the one contractual obligation — cannot be fully proven.** The chain
   terminates in supplier heat, which has no source anywhere.
3. **`SC-072` is designed to fail.** If it is later "fixed" by widening the tolerance rather than
   correcting the basis, the evidence for `CL-08` disappears and the defect ships.
4. **The simulator's fidelity is unproven** (`G39`). Every real-time and PLC scenario in this plan runs
   against a model built from our own assumptions. Green tests here do not predict commissioning.
5. **Coverage percentages have no agreed denominator** until `CL-45` reconciles the three requirement
   totals.

## 20. Recommendations

### 20.1 Before test design begins

1. **Answer the 13 Blocker clarifications** (`CL-01`–`CL-13`). Nine are already registered as `Q##` or
   `OI-##` — this is a chase, not a discovery exercise. **`CL-01` first**: without it, Phase 4 has no
   demonstrable happy path.
2. **Decide `CL-03` (refuse versus authorise) and `CL-04` (FL2 live versus null).** Both are direct
   contradictions between live `Must` text, and both block whole scenario families. ⛔ **Do not edit
   `FR-120` on `Q19`'s strength before asking** — the current text is at least self-consistent across six
   documents.
3. **Re-grain the tolerance model before seeding anything** (`CL-05`). Seeding per-alloy makes `SC-011`
   pass against wrong data, which is worse than a failing test.
4. **Get §5.25–§5.30 client-reviewed as a block** — 69 `Must` requirements carrying the shared-schema
   write-back, the allocation model and the coil identity design.

### 20.2 Sequencing advice for the Test Design Agent

- **Design P0 first, and design the failure cases before the happy paths.** On this module the happy path
  is the least informative test: the register's own defects cluster in partial failure, contradiction and
  persistence, not in the main flow.
- **Treat route as a dimension, not a parameter.** A case proven on FL1 does not transfer to FL2 or FL3 —
  the three differ in what exists, what is broadcast, and how many controllers one acknowledgement writes
  to.
- **Do not design cases for `FR-381`–`FR-387` as published.** All five are superseded on the arithmetic;
  designing to them would assert known-wrong behaviour.
- **Do not design server-side role-enforcement cases for MVP-1.** Nothing can return a `403`. Design
  `SC-158` as the assertion of that condition instead.
- **Where a scenario is marked ⛔, design the *characterisation* case, not an assertion.** An exploratory
  or observation-only case records what the build does; it must not invent an expected result.
- **Use named data categories and placeholders, never invented values**, for every value listed as
  undefined in §11 — tolerance bands, N, weld joint limit, spool target weight, dwell, latency budget.

### 20.3 Dependencies the design pass will hit immediately

| Dependency | Impact if unmet |
|---|---|
| A seeded `Active` pass schedule set | No check-in case can be executed |
| The shared instance `DEV00164-001`, not LocalDB | Cross-database atomicity cases silently pass while proving nothing |
| A working `WipRejection` seed | `G108` — the insert has been failing silently; every WIP case must verify its own fixture |
| `SpoolOrder` and `DieHistory` fixtures | Written by nothing (`G109`, `G115`); must be created directly |
| A multi-rod spool fixture | Required for BO2. ⚠ `G42` — `SpoolProcessing` cannot represent multi-rod genealogy |
| `ng build shared` before dependent runs | Jest resolves `shared` to `dist/`, not source |
| The test-only `OPCConnection` double | The only route to integration-level coverage |

### 20.4 Unresolved concerns to carry forward

- **The absence of an integration test level is a strategy gap, not a planning gap.** `D-50` reinstated
  the .NET unit level only. Contract verification is manual inspection. This plan works within that; it
  does not endorse it.
- **`FR-563` and `NFR012` mean the module can be feature-complete and still unable to issue a
  certificate.** That should be visible on the release dashboard, not discovered at the first customer
  shipment.
- **A six-column permission matrix will be reviewed with the client.** `[SEC]` itself asks that the MVP-1
  position be said out loud. QA should not let a demonstration imply enforcement that `SC-158` proves is
  absent.

### 20.5 Handoff boundary to the Test Design Agent

**What is handed over:** scope and out-of-scope areas, the risk register with test responses, the coverage
strategy and depth tiers, justified design techniques, test-data categories, database validation needs,
integration boundaries and failure modes, regression impact, **178 high-level scenarios** with coverage
type, risk and priority, 50 clarifications with severity, and full requirement traceability including
uncovered items.

**What is deliberately not handed over:** test steps, per-case expected results, test data values, SQL,
endpoint definitions, and any implementation-specific assertion. Where the sources state a value it is
named in this plan; where they do not, a clarification is raised and **no value has been chosen on the
sources' behalf**.

**What the design pass must not do:** create tests for withdrawn scope; design to superseded formulas;
invent an expected result for a ⛔ scenario; assume an integration suite exists; or convert a
`[PROPOSED]` requirement into a confirmed one by testing it.
